the genes that determine the root plasticity response of a single Arabidiopsis accession to distinct environments are the same genes that control the natural variation in root allometry among accessions.
the genes controlling natural variation in root system architecture also mediate the phenotypic responses of a plant to its environment.
the genetic mechanisms underlying adaptation across natural populations also determine the plasticity responses within individuals.

the genetic mechanisms that control the plasticity of root systems in Arabidopsis thaliana and the role of such plasticity in the evolution of root system architecture.

the genetic mechanisms underlying the phenotypically plastic response of an individual to distinct environments and the genetic basis for natural variation across populations.

the genetic mechanisms that determine natural variation also underlie phenotypic plastic responses within a population.
the genetic architecture underlying root plasticity within an accession is largely similar to that of root architecture across accessions.

our integrative plasticity space approach, which is based on the phenotypic variation of root systems, provides a powerful tool to identify candidate genes underlying the genetic architecture of root plasticity and phenotypic variation across natural accessions.

natural variation in root system architecture (RSA) across Arabidopsis thaliana accessions is mediated by the plasticity response of a single genotype to distinct environments.
the genetic mechanisms that control natural variation in root phenotypes across populations also determine plasticity within a population.

the same genes that underlie phenotypic diversity in Arabidopsis populations are also involved in the plastic response of individuals to their environments.
